bull.b: Debt of only about $2.5M and a debt-to-equity ratio near 0.01 leave relatively little fixed financing burden. That supports resilience and preserves flexibility to direct capital toward oncology development rather than mandatory interest and principal payments.

Equity rose from negative levels in 2021–2023 to about $323.1M TTM, after reaching $411.1M in 2025, showing that capital raises materially strengthened capitalization. This cushion can support continued development and absorb operating losses over the medium term.

The company is funding its cash burn without relying on debt, consistent with its very low leverage. That reduces refinancing exposure and avoids adding interest obligations, giving management more flexibility while the oncology pipeline remains in development.

bear.b: Zero revenue confirms that BBOT has not yet established commercial product sales or internal operating funding. The company therefore remains dependent on capital markets or other financing while it advances its oncology programs, limiting near-term financial self-sufficiency.

The widening net loss indicates that operating costs are growing faster than any progress toward commercialization. Losses of $182.1M on a TTM basis can erode the capital base and increase the amount of financing required before the business can generate sustainable earnings.

Deeply negative and worsening operating and free cash flow show that reported losses are translating into substantial cash outflows. Continued burn increases external financing needs and creates ongoing dilution risk even though the balance sheet currently carries little debt.
